                This is also highly relevant from a $ALAB perspective.

Marvell is emphasizing CXL, PCIe scale-up, memory bandwidth, low latency, and fabric connectivity at #FMS2026.

In other words, the bottleneck in next-generation AI infrastructure is expanding beyond GPUs themselves to memory + connectivity.

And when it comes to scale-up switching, $ALAB is already ahead with Scorpio moving into production.

Marvell is clearly targeting the same massive opportunity, but for now, Astera Labs appears to have the first-mover advantage.

If anything, seeing a major competitor like Marvell emphasize these exact areas reinforces just how large the opportunity could be for ALAB’s Leo / Scorpio / Aries portfolio. 🚀

                【Why I Don’t Invest in Memory Stocks】

I’m not saying memory stocks have no more upside.

But I believe the bottlenecks in AI infrastructure are gradually moving outward from the XPU.

XPU
↓
HBM
↓
PCIe / CXL
↓
Scale-up
↓
Multi-rack
↓
Scale-out
↓
Optics

The HBM shortage will continue.

But that’s increasingly becoming consensus.

Meanwhile, as AI clusters grow larger, connectivity, networking, and optics become increasingly critical — and their addressable markets could expand far beyond current expectations.

That’s why I’d rather invest in companies positioned to solve the next bottlenecks to emerge, rather than the ones everyone can already see.

I believe the biggest asymmetry between future market size and current market capitalization may actually lie further down the stack.
